verdict.rationale: Terraform acts on many resources in one run: plan and apply cover the whole configuration, parallelize non-dependent resources, can destroy all remote objects with -destroy, and one import block can import several resources at once. Bulk refactoring is weaker, though: a community user reports that moving hundreds or thousands of resources via state mv is a big job, and there are no documented first-party bulk selectors or filters for state operations. missing for 10: documented bulk/filtered state manipulation (mass move or remove), first-party docs for for_each-style fan-out, independent hands-on corroboration of large-scale bulk runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: Terraform builds a graph of all your resources, and parallelizes the creation and modification of any non-dependent resources.
You can specify multiple resources in the `import` block to import more than one resource at a time.
These include `-destroy`, which creates a plan to destroy all remote objects
You can pass the `-auto-approve` option to instruct Terraform to apply the plan without asking for confirmation.
